# tenable-axi investigation guide

Investigate Tenable One exposure and run explicitly guarded writes.
Start with the relevant read below, without running help first.
Examples use synthetic values; replace them with evidence from the current investigation.
Use the installed binary or the shown non-interactive package invocation.
Append `--profile <name>` and optionally `--config <file>` to select an existing profile.
Run npx -y @knowttl/tenable-axi config path; configure a profile with accessKey and secretKey SecretRefs.
Credentials use environment/file SecretRefs, never inline secrets or arguments.
Only `https://cloud.tenable.com` is supported.

## Investigation reads

Each line is an independent example, not a startup sequence.
The fields shown are useful compact projections; omit `--fields` for the command's compact defaults.

| Task | Exact example |
|---|---|
| Check credentials locally, without HTTP | `npx -y @knowttl/tenable-axi auth status` |
| Look up an asset by text | `npx -y @knowttl/tenable-axi asset list --query example-device --class DEVICE --limit 10 --fields id,name,class,exposureScore` |
| Read one exact asset, including observation evidence | `npx -y @knowttl/tenable-axi asset show --id asset-1 --fields id,name,fqdns,last_observed_at` |
| Pivot from an asset ID to findings | `npx -y @knowttl/tenable-axi finding list --filter 'asset_id = ["asset-1"]' --limit 20 --fields id,name,severity,state,sensor_type,cves` |
| Search high severity findings | `npx -y @knowttl/tenable-axi finding list --filter 'severity = ["HIGH"]' --filter 'sensor_type = ["NESSUS"]' --limit 20` |
| Read a finding and its asset/CVE evidence | `npx -y @knowttl/tenable-axi finding show --id finding-1 --fields id,name,severity,state,asset_id,cves,sensor_type` |
| Count severity and sensor values | `npx -y @knowttl/tenable-axi finding summary` |
| Find installed software | `npx -y @knowttl/tenable-axi software list --query example-app --limit 10 --fields name,version,publisher` |
| Discover asset filter properties | `npx -y @knowttl/tenable-axi asset properties --asset-classes DEVICE --limit 20 --fields key,operators,filterable,sortable` |
| Discover finding filter properties | `npx -y @knowttl/tenable-axi finding properties --limit 20 --fields key,operators,filterable,sortable` |
| Discover software filter properties | `npx -y @knowttl/tenable-axi software properties --limit 20 --fields key,operators,filterable,sortable` |
| Find high priority paths for an asset | `npx -y @knowttl/tenable-axi attack-path list --filter 'asset_id eq "asset-1"' --filter 'priority gte 8' --limit 10 --fields id,name,priority,summary` |
| Read techniques and affected asset IDs together | `npx -y @knowttl/tenable-axi attack-technique list --limit 10 --fields id,name,affectedAssets,assets_ids,mitre_id` |
| Read exposure cards | `npx -y @knowttl/tenable-axi card list --limit 5 --fields id,name,score` |
| Find Exposure Management tags | `npx -y @knowttl/tenable-axi tag list --query example --limit 10` |
| Diagnose failed connector syncs | `npx -y @knowttl/tenable-axi connector logs --status FAILED --start-date 2026-01-01 --end-date 2026-02-01 --limit 10` |
| Wait for an existing attack export | `npx -y @knowttl/tenable-axi export attack status --id 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 --wait` |

Inventory filters are repeatable AND conditions with a JSON array of strings, even for numeric values.
Inventory `--filter-file` accepts a flat JSON array and excludes `--filter`.
Attack filters instead use `eq`, `gte`, etc. with a JSON scalar or array; resolved records are excluded unless `--include-resolved` is set.
Connector dates must be paired: start inclusive, end exclusive.
Connector defaults include sync identity, trigger, first failed stage and first error; request `--full` only if text is truncated.

## Save calls and bound output

Use list `--fields` to retrieve the needed evidence together instead of showing every result.
Inventory selected extra fields are requested automatically; `--extra-properties` also adds them to output.
Exact-ID `asset show` and `finding show` search directly without a preceding list.
`finding summary` is one CLI call making 19 sequential limit-1 reads without retries, using upstream totals.
It has no filters or per-asset grouping; counts are independent, sensor values may overlap, and `complete: false` means partial counts.

Ordinary lists default to 100 rows; use `--limit 1..10000` or `--all` (at most 10,000 rows, incompatible with `--limit`).
Inventory/attack collection reads share 20-second, 20-request and 20 MiB decoded-response budgets.
Check `count`, `total` (possibly null), `complete`, `reason` and any `error` before concluding absence.
Resume a returned `--cursor` with the same profile, filters, fields and sort; do not combine it with `--offset`.
`--full` removes the 1,000-character text preview, without adding fields, rows or budget.
Connector logs have no server paging; `UPSTREAM_UNPAGED` means unavailable history, not an exhaustive empty result.

Attack export status `--wait` polls once per second within 20 seconds/20 requests; inspect the returned state before downloading.
There is no combined export start-and-wait, inventory-status wait, bulk show or asset-to-findings pivot command.
Use a filtered list for multiple details; use the returned asset ID in a separate finding query.
Software has no stable ID or show command.

## Read allowlist and state changes

The table above is read-only, including POST searches and waiting on an existing export.
Other remote reads: `home`, `card show`, `tag properties`, platform `tag category/value list/show`, `tag assignment/exclusion/asset-filter list`, `initiative list/show`, `combination list/show/filters`, `export asset/finding jobs`, `export inventory status` and `doctor`.
`doctor` makes eight module probes without retries; use it for access diagnosis, not before each case.
Local reads: `auth status`, `profile list`, `config path`, `hook`, help and version.
Configured home reads up to five live cards; the optional hook reads local posture only.

Exclude all `create/update/delete/bulk-delete`, `tag assignment add/remove` and `export * start` commands from read allowlists.
Writes require a file profile's `allowWrites` and exact operation allowlist even for previews, followed by `--execute` and the exact preview `--confirm` string.
`TENABLE_AXI_READ_ONLY=true` forces read-only.
Export downloads read remotely but create a local file at an explicit new output path; `setup hooks` changes local integration files and needs explicit installation intent.
Users, roles, access control, credential minting and arbitrary HTTP are unavailable.

## Help and failures

Use help to recover from a failed or unfamiliar command, not to start an investigation.
Top-level `--help` returns the command index, home flags and version aliases.
Leaf `--help` returns that command's flags, defaults, required selectors and examples (plus default fields where applicable).
Group-only help such as `asset --help` is unsupported and returns a usage error with valid commands.
The [command reference](https://github.com/knowttl/tenable-axi/blob/main/docs/commands.md) lists the full surface.

Stdout is structured TOON, including errors and actionable help.
Exit 0 means success (still inspect completeness), 1 means operation/configuration failure, and 2 means CLI usage validation failure.

| Code | Adjustment |
|---|---|
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Fix selectors, flag spelling or filter grammar using the returned hint; upstream validation can exit 1. |
| `CONFIG_INVALID`, `CONFIG_INSECURE` | Fix the profile/SecretRefs or private file permissions; use a complete credential pair and the supported origin. |
| `AUTH_REQUIRED` (401) | Repair credentials through the approved secret source; do not repeat unchanged requests. |
| `PERMISSION_DENIED` (403) | Check licensing and the operation's privilege; inventory access does not imply attack or connector access. |
| `NOT_FOUND` | Verify the exact ID and selected profile; a zero-row list is instead a successful search. |
| `RATE_LIMITED`, `REQUEST_FAILED`, `TRANSPORT_FAILED` | Reads already retry 429/502/503/504 up to twice within budgets; honor `retryAfter` milliseconds and investigate persistent failure. |
| `RESPONSE_INVALID` | Treat the result as invalid or partial, preserve evidence and report the mismatch. |
| `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`, `REQUEST_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, `BYTE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, `ROW_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` | Narrow filters/fields or resume a supplied cursor; never infer completeness. |
| `EXPORT_NOT_READY` | Inspect job state before downloading; status waiting does not guarantee completion. |
| `OPERATION_BLOCKED`, `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` | Respect write guards; for unknown mutation outcomes follow the audit ID and read-back advice, never replay blindly. |
